cases.source: The Professional Team reviewed the methodology for landfall updates by gate and by category.
The Professional Team reviewed the methodology for landfall updates by gate and by category.
The Professional Team examined the calculations for historical coastal landfall frequencies.
The Professional Team inspected the coastal gates map and Form S-3 and marked the standard Verified: YES.
The reviewers assessed the smoothing of historical frequencies and recorded no requested change.
The Professional Team reviewed the gate-by-category updates and accepted the submitted explanation.
The Professional Team challenged the coastal landfall method and requested a revised calculation.
The reviewers identified a deficiency in the landfall frequency method and required RMS to correct it.
The Professional Team instructed RMS to change its smoothing method before acceptance.
The reviewers rejected the submitted coastal-frequency method because it did not satisfy the standard.
The Professional Team issued a formal objection to the gate-specific calibration and demanded a response.
The reviewers found the methodology inconsistent with the requirement and directed the vendor to revise it.
The Professional Team reviewed the coastal landfall method. RMS also reported an update to the event set. The documents do not link the update to the review.
At the opening briefing, RMS listed the event-set update as already completed. The Professional Team examined the method later in the review.
The reviewers verified the standard. The vendor submission describes its smoothing method but gives no response to a review request.
After the review meeting, RMS updated its coastal landfall methodology. The document does not state why the update was made.
In response to the Professional Team's request to correct coastal-frequency calculations, RMS revised those calculations.
The review report instructed RMS to revise its coastal landfall method; RMS's written response states that it changed the method because of that instruction.
